:::{#thm-cross-entropy-discrete}
#### Cross-entropy of two mass functions

Let $p$ and $q$ be [probability mass functions](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) on $\set{1, \ldots, K}$,
with $p_k$ and $q_k$ the probabilities of outcome $k$.
Then the [cross-entropy](#def-cross-entropy) is

$$\crossentropyf{p}{q} = -\sumto{k}{K} p_k \log q_k.$$

A term with $p_k = 0$ is taken to be $0$
whatever $q_k$ is,
as for [entropy](#thm-entropy-discrete).

:::

::: proof

Let $X$ have [mass function](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) $p$,
and let $g(k) \eqdef -\log q_k$,
so that $-\log q(X) = g(X)$.
First suppose $q_k > 0$
whenever $p_k > 0$.
Then $g(k)$ is finite for every value $k$ that $X$ takes with positive [probability](probability-basics.qmd#def-probability),
and [LOTUS](#thm-lotus) gives

$$
\ba
\crossentropyf{p}{q}
&= \E{g(X)} && \text{(definition)} \\
&= \sum_{k : p_k > 0} g(k) \cd \P(X = k) && \text{(LOTUS)} \\
&= -\sum_{k : p_k > 0} p_k \log q_k && \text{(definition of } g \text{ and } \P(X = k) = p_k \text{)} \\
&= -\sumto{k}{K} p_k \log q_k. && \text{(terms with } p_k = 0 \text{ are } 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

Now suppose $q_k = 0$ for some $k$ with $p_k > 0$.
Then $-\log q(X) \ge 0$,
and $-\log q(X) = \infty$ with probability at least $p_k > 0$,
so $\crossentropyf{p}{q} = \infty$.
The right side is also $\infty$,
because its term for $k$ is $-p_k \log 0 = \infty$
and its other terms are finite or $\infty$ but never $-\infty$.

:::
